title: Equal sea heat anomalies decreased Landsat kelp canopy only in the California Current among 14 regions in 1985-2026, and a 1985-2013 heat model explained 9-41% of the later loss there
abstract: Question: does the same marine heat dose give the same kelp canopy loss in different regions, and is the loss controlled by the local SST anomaly or by an absolute warm limit? Data: quarterly Landsat kelp canopy area (Kelpwatch.org) for 163 coastal segments of about 45 km in 14 regions of both hemispheres (SE Alaska to Baja California, Kamchatka-Kuril, Patagonia, Falklands, Namibia and South Africa), with monthly NOAA OISST v2.1. Method: the response was the log ratio of the peak-season canopy to its 1984-2013 median; heat was the peak monthly anomaly or the peak absolute SST in the prior 12 months. We compared no-heat, anomaly, absolute-hinge and combined models by leave-one-region-out and forward (fit 1985-2013, test 2014-2026) tests. Results: within-segment slopes per +1 C were negative only in northern California (-0.59, 95% interval -0.85 to -0.36), Baja California (-0.31), southern California (-0.29) and central California (-0.17). In the other 10 regions all intervals included zero; the Western Cape (warmest month 18.6 C) had -0.01 (-0.09 to 0.07). The regional slope did not follow regional warmth (Spearman rho -0.01, n = 14). Heat models reduced mean regional error by at most 3% against a no-heat model in leave-one-region-out and forward tests, with intervals that included zero; an absolute hinge at 20 C was not better than the anomaly model. The frozen anomaly model explained 26%, 41%, 37% and 9% of the 2014-2026 canopy loss in Baja, southern, central and northern California; within 2014-2026 the heat slope there was near zero, so the loss acted as a level shift. Observation bias: segment-years with fewer than three cloud-free quarters were 0.19 log units lower (SE 0.04), and before 1999 most non-US regions had almost no Landsat data. With only 1999-2026 full-coverage years, SE Alaska and the Falklands also had small negative slopes. Limitations: SST at 0.25 degrees, no nitrate, wave or urchin data, non-US kelp layers end in 2021-2025 with unpublished methods, and possible sensor steps in 2012-2013.

display.caption: Within-segment slope of the kelp canopy response per +1 C peak SST anomaly by region, against the climatological warmest-month SST. Filled: main sample (1985-2026, clear fraction at least 0.5). Open: 1999-2026 full-coverage segment-years only. Bars: 95% year-block bootstrap intervals. Only the four California Current regions have clear negative slopes.

Median segment canopy response by region and year (solid) and the forward prediction of a pooled anomaly model fitted to 1985-2013 (dashed). Shaded: test years 2014-2026. The model misses most of the California Current loss after 2014. Very low early values in Kamchatka-Kuril and Tierra del Fuego come from years with almost no Landsat 5 data.

Mean canopy response in 1 C bins of peak absolute SST (left) and 0.5 C bins of peak anomaly (right) by hemisphere, with 95% intervals (bins with at least 20 segment-years). Dashed: pooled absolute hinge fit (threshold 20 C).

citations.reason: Marine heatwaves gave no general assemblage change in BioTIME; we find no general kelp canopy response outside the California Current.
Frozen climate relations rarely capture later level shifts; the kelp heat model explained 9-41% of the post-2014 California Current loss.
